tonight.headline: Lost, 103.8 to 140.6. 0-3, and Achane is out for the season
body: De'Von Achane tore his ACL on Sunday and will miss the rest of the season (CBS Sports, citing ESPN and NFL Media, 28 Sep 10:49 ET). That landed after this morning's brief. Your week was already lost: every starter is final at 103.8 against Footballers' 140.6, and you're 0-3.

There's one thing to do before Wednesday 01:00 Mexico City: put in a claim for Ollie Gordon II and drop Achane (card below). Chem has no IR slot, so Achane is now a dead roster spot. After tonight's game, Tuten takes Achane's RB slot.

case.label: What changed since this morning
case.body: Achane: torn ACL, out for the season (CBS, 28 Sep). Jefferson: the MRI showed a sprained ankle and he might play Sunday against Miami (Yardbarker, citing NFL Network and ESPN). Coker: a minor quad strain, and he could play Week 4 against Detroit depending on Wednesday-Friday practice (CBS). Allen's knee isn't viewed as a concern (RotoWire, 28 Sep).

case.label: Was the lineup wrong?
case.body: No. The lineup as set was the projection lineup (136.6, gap 0.0) and every starter was active at kickoff. Three got hurt during the game. Tuten (17.0) and McLaurin (19.7) outscored them from the bench, but only hindsight picks those swaps, and you lost by 36.8.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Nothing for Week 3; it's final. For Week 4, the Gordon claim clearing and the Week 4 projections once the week rolls after tonight.

doFirst.deadlineLabel: Claims process Wed 01:00 Mexico City (07:00 UTC)
doFirst.title: Claim Ollie Gordon II, drop De'Von Achane
doFirst.subtitle: Achane is out for the season with a torn ACL and Chem has no IR slot. Gordon played 84% of Miami's snaps once he went down.

case.label: The news
case.body: Achane tore his ACL on a first-quarter cut at Miami on Sunday and will miss the rest of the 2026 season (CBS Sports, citing ESPN and NFL Media, 28 Sep 10:49 ET). This broke after this morning's brief and after Week 3's projections, so nothing in the snapshot prices it.

case.label: The role
case.body: Gordon played 83.6% of Miami's snaps after the injury: 20 carries for 48 yards and a touchdown, plus 14 receiving yards (DraftKings Network, 28 Sep). He'd had three touches in two weeks before that (CBS).

case.label: The drop
case.body: Achane, 99.8% rostered. That's a market disagreement on the record, and the reason is simple: he's out for the season, and Chem's lineup has no IR slot (slot 21 count is 0), so he holds a roster spot and can't score. Nobody else on the roster gets touched. Kamara keeps his seat because Etienne's hamstring gives him the Saints' lead-back work (CBS).

case.label: The contested part
case.body: DraftKings Network calls both Miami backs fringe options and says most managers should avoid the backfield: Miami are 0-3 and 31st in scoring. Hafley says 'they're all going to have their roles', and Jaylen Wright (foot, stinger) missed Week 3 but may return. I take the claim anyway because the cost is a dead roster spot. It's depth, not a starter, and the card is SOLID, not ELITE.

case.label: The priority
case.body: AVIATO is 10th of 10 in waiver order in this snapshot. Chem's order resets weekly, so the claim costs nothing lasting, but any rival who claims him first gets him. ESPN won't show you rival claims.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Wright returns and Gordon draws under 12 touches in Week 4, which would make this a timeshare. Or Monangai outscores Gordon in two of Weeks 4-6, which would say the seat was better spent elsewhere.

case.label: The trigger
case.body: This card fired if Achane was ruled out for Week 4. He's out for the season: torn ACL (CBS Sports, 28 Sep 10:49 ET).

case.label: Why Tuten
case.body: Jacksonville's starter: 15 carries, 73 yards and a TD plus 2 catches on Sunday, and 43 carries for 204 yards through three games (Jaguars.com). Coen: 'He has been a pro's pro.' His snap share has held at 48-50% all season (PFF).

case.label: Where the projection decides
case.body: Kamara may project close once Week 4 rolls, because Etienne is ruled out for the Falcons game (CBS). If the Week 4 projection puts Kamara more than two points ahead, start Kamara instead. Within two points it's a coin flip: take the projection and move on.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: The back you start is outscored by the best RB left on your bench in Week 4. Graded on the outcome from the archive.

doFirst.deadlineLabel: WHEN THE WEEK ROLLS · only if Coker or Jefferson is out for Week 4
doFirst.title: If Coker or Jefferson can't go: McLaurin starts, then Boston
doFirst.subtitle: Not armed, and less likely than it was: Jefferson has a sprain and might play; Coker's quad is a minor strain and he could play against Detroit.

case.label: The injuries
case.body: Jefferson: the MRI confirmed a sprained left ankle and he 'might suit up' against Miami on Sunday (Yardbarker, citing NFL Network and ESPN, 28 Sep). Coker: a minor quadriceps strain; he could play against the Lions, and Wednesday-Friday practice decides (CBS Sports, 28 Sep).

case.label: Why McLaurin first
case.body: Two straight weeks of 9 targets from Mariota, and PFF note he kept the top receiver role with Daniels out. Daniels is expected back in three weeks or sooner with no IR (The Big Lead, 27 Sep), so Mariota very likely starts Week 4 against the Colts.

case.label: Then Boston
case.body: Cleveland's X receiver: over 90% of snaps in 11 and 12 personnel (PFF). Two catches for 41 on Sunday.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Both receivers practise fully by Friday, and the card never fires. If it fires, it's graded on the outcome: McLaurin against the man he replaced.

whatWentWrong.title: Achane is gone for the season, and two more starters got hurt
whatWentWrong.lead: Achane tore his ACL. Coker (quad strain) and Jefferson (ankle sprain) look minor. All three were started correctly.

case.label: Not a lineup miss
case.body: The lineup as set was the projection lineup and every starter was active at kickoff. The three scored 10.7 on 51.5 projected.

case.label: What it changes
case.body: Achane's ACL (CBS, 28 Sep) turns a RB1 into a dead roster spot with no IR slot to park him in. Both cards above follow from it: claim Gordon with Achane as the drop, and Tuten into the lineup.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Nothing for Achane. Coker and Jefferson are Wednesday's practice reports.

whatWentWrong.sources: CBS Sports · Yardbarker · ESPN league file

whatWentWrong.title: The Coker-over-McLaurin flex call lost, 3.8 to 19.7
whatWentWrong.lead: Closed WRONG. The falsifier fired: Coker got 4 targets while Mariota threw McLaurin 9.

case.label: The call
case.body: On 21 Sep the brief moved Coker into the flex because Daniels' injury meant Mariota would start. The falsifier said the call was wrong if Coker drew under five targets while McLaurin drew eight or more. Coker got 4 before the quad took him out (The Big Lead). McLaurin got 9 (NBC).

case.label: The honest part
case.body: The injury cut Coker's day short, and that doesn't rescue the call. A lineup decision is graded on its outcome, and this one lost by 15.9. The theory that Mariota would starve McLaurin was wrong on its first test.

case.label: What it changes
case.body: The flex slot reopens. Week 4's projection decides it, and the second card makes McLaurin the first replacement if a receiver is out.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: The Week 3 archive disagreeing with the reported target counts. The archive grades it formally once it's published.

waiverAnalysis.summary: Nothing on the wire beats this roster on usage. Monangai (RB) and Boston (WR) are the weakest players you could move, and nobody on the wire clears either. The sample is two weeks, which is thin, and it can't see Sunday: Ollie Gordon's role started when Achane went down, so he's the claim card above on injury news, not a tool result.
